text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Talks on alliance between Rabobank and PVF pension fund halted after the two parties failed to reach an agreement. (p1)
- Dutch PTT KPN expects further profits growth after announcing nine percent 1996 net profit rise. (p1)
- EOE options exchange to move in with the Amsterdam stock exchange this year. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers gets consent for his bill on competition after concession to parliament. (p1)
- Grocery wholesaler De Boer Winkelbedrijven reports boosted market share in all areas of activity in 1996. (p3)
- Information technology firm Simac is expecting 30 percent profits growth this year. (p3)
- Generale Bank Nederland (GBN), subsidiary of Generale Bank of Belgium, books 43.2 pct profit increase, largely due to lower costs. (p4)
- Investment company Manaus plans to compete with KPN's telecom arm PTT Telecom. (p4) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Half of the house owners will have to pay extra tax on their houses next year. (p1)
- Bank insurer ING Group blockades merger between Belgium's banks Generale Bank and Bank Brussel Lambert (BBL). (p2)
- Amsterdam stock exchange had to close early on Tuesday due to technical trouble. (p2)
- Waste disposal unit of utility company Edon takes 49 pct stake in rival VAM. (p19) DE TELEGRAAF
- Strikes threaten in the building sector as employers and unions seem way off an accord. (p7)
- Industrial group Stork makes concession in bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker's relaunch talks. (p21)
- Textile group Braat Beheer deep in the red due to restructuring costs. (p23) TROUW
- Christian Democrats party is looking outside politics for someone to head list of candidates for next year's election. (p1)
- Brewer Heineken's net profit under pressure of lower beer consumption. (p6) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Office supply firm Ahrend books higher 1996 net at Dfl 41.8 million. (p11)
